chunks: Ḥamzah ibn Ḥumrān asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about the one who says:
"Release me where You have prevented me."
So he said: "He is released where Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has prevented him.
He said: "Did he not say that? And the stipulation does not remove from him the Hajj in the following year."

key_terms.الِاشْتِرَاطُ: The stipulation made upon entering iḥrām
key_terms.حَيْثُ حَبَسْتَنِي: At the place where You prevent or detain me
key_terms.حُلَّنِي: Release me from the state of iḥrām

ai.seo_question: Does making a condition at iḥrām remove the obligation to perform Hajj later if one is prevented?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning the pilgrim who stipulates at iḥrām that he will exit if prevented. If he is obstructed, he becomes released at the place where Allah has prevented him. However, this condition does not exempt him from the obligation of performing Hajj in a later year.
